title: Empty object, empty array and explicit null at depth, plus an empty chain
rationale: ValueDomainContractTest pins the flatten-side collapse of {} / [] / null. This extends it to the reconstruct side and to depth: the collapse is not repaired anywhere downstream, and the reconstructed document actively asserts null where the source asserted an empty container.
catchesBugClass: That the known flatten-side collapse is not compensated during reconstruction and survives arbitrary depth. Also guards the accepted half - if a future fix preserves emptiness by dropping the terminal key, this catches the depth regression.
cannotCatch: It cannot distinguish the three collapsed inputs from each other after flattening - they are byte-identical, so no reconstructor-only change can pass it. It also does not cover an empty container as the ROOT document.

predicted.detail: Three distinct container states collapse to one null. The ACCEPTED half holds: nesting depth of the empty chain is preserved exactly.
